releases.name: Just the Browser v1.8
releases.body:
This update contains changes to the **Microsoft Edge** configuration. You can [install Just the Browser](https://justthebrowser.com/) again to get the latest version. Existing users on other browsers do not need to update, unless the settings are not working.

### Configuration settings
- Microsoft Edge's [Copilot Cowork](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/cowork/cowork-local-browser) integration is now disabled
- Manifest V2 support in Microsoft Edge is now force-enabled, so uBlock Origin and other MV2 extensions should keep working until support is [completely removed in 2027](https://blogs.windows.com/msedgedev/2026/08/07/moving-the-microsoft-edge-extensions-ecosystem-forward-with-manifest-version-3/)

### Installation scripts
- Fixed Google Chrome detection on Arch Linux (#73)

releases.name: Just the Browser v1.6
releases.body:
This update contains changes to the **Firefox** and **Edge** configurations, you can [install Just the Browser](https://justthebrowser.com/) again to get the latest version. Existing users on other browsers do not need to update, unless the settings are not working.

### Configuration settings
- Firefox's built-in VPN is now explicitly allowed, since it's usually disabled when group policies are installed
- Edge is now blocked from asking to import data from other browsers
- Edge will no longer show "Ask Copilot" suggestions in the search bar (#57)
- Edge is now blocked from sharing personalized data for advertising, search, news, Microsoft Edge, and other Microsoft services
- Edge's floating desktop Search Bar is now blocked, since it prevents Edge from fully shutting down on Windows

### Installation scripts
- Fixed detection for Firefox Flatpak on Linux

readmeExcerpt:
# Just the Browser

Just the Browser helps you remove AI features, telemetry data reporting, sponsored content, product integrations, and other annoyances from desktop web browsers. The goal is to give you "just the browser" and nothing else, using hidden settings in web browsers intended for companies and other organizations.

This project includes configuration files for popular web browsers, documentation for installing and modifying them, and easy installation scripts.



## Install script

The setup script can install the configuration files in a few clicks. You can also follow the manual guides for [Google Chrome](/chrome), [Microsoft Edge](/edge), [Firefox](/firefox), and [Brave](/brave). If you don't like running scripts with administrator/root access, or the script does not work, use the guides instead.

**Windows:** Search for "Windows PowerShell" in the Start Menu, right-click it, and select the "Run as administrator" option. Next, copy the below command, paste it into the window (`Ctrl+V`), and press the Enter/Return key:
```
& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/corbindavenport/just-the-browser/main/main.ps1")))
```
If you are on older versions of Windows, you may need to run this command first:
```
[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol=[Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12
```

**Mac and Linux:** Search for the Terminal in your applications list and open it. Next, copy the below command, paste it into the window (`Ctrl+V` or `Cmd+V`), and press the Enter/Return key:

```
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/corbindavenport/just-the-browser/main/main.sh)"
```


## Documentation and config files

See the [Google Chrome](chrome/README.md), [Microsoft Edge](edge/README.md), [Mozilla Firefox](firefox/README.md), and [Brave](brave/README.md) documentation pages for manual installation instructions, and explanations for each setting. The browser directories also contain the configuration files, which are either JSON files, [Windows Registry .reg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Registry#.REG_files) files for Windows, or [Profile Manager .mobileconfig](https://support.apple.com/guide/profile-manager/distribute-profiles-manually-pmdbd71ebc9/mac) files for macOS.

## Website

This repository also includes the static site generator for [justthebrowser.com](https://justthebrowser.com/), built with [Eleventy](https://www.11ty.dev/) and [Simple.css](https://simplecss.org/). The icons are from [Bootstrap Icons](https://icons.getbootstrap.com/).

With Node.js and NPM installed, you can test the site like this:

```shell
npm install
npx @11ty/eleventy --serve
```

The site is compiled and deployed with the `eleventy_build.yml` GitHub Action.

## Subscribe to updates

You can subscribe to the RSS/Atom releases feed to know when the configuration files, documentation, and scripts are updated:

```
https://github.com/corbindavenport/just-the-browser/releases.atom
```

This feed can be used with [Feedly](https://feedly.com/i/subscription/feed%2Fhttps%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fcorbindavenport%2Fjust-the-browser%2Freleases.atom), [Inoreader](https://www.inoreader.com/?add_feed=https://github.com/corbindavenport/just-the-browser/releases.atom), [The Old Reader](https://theoldreader.com/feeds/subscribe?url=https://github.com/corbindavenport/just-the-browser/releases.atom), [Feedbin](https://feedbin.me/?subscribe=https://github.com/corbindavenport/just-the-browser/releases.atom), or any other reader tool. You can also subscribe to new releases with your GitHub account by clicking the Watch button at the top of the page, then selecting Custom > New releases.

aiSummary.oneLiner: Configuration scripts utilizing enterprise policies to strip AI integrations and telemetry from major desktop browsers.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Just the Browser is a collection of configuration files and scripts designed to aggressively debloat popular desktop web browsers. It functions by exploiting hidden, enterprise-level organizational policies to forcefully disable built-in AI assistants, background telemetry reporting, sponsored content, and unnecessary product integrations. The project provides specifically tailored configurations for Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Firefox, and Brave. By applying these strict policies across Windows, macOS, or Linux, it forces the applications to act solely as rendering engines, returning users to a clean, highly minimalist, and distraction-free browsing experience.
keyFeatures: Enterprise policy enforcement: Leverages legitimate organizational administrative settings to permanently disable unwanted consumer features.
Cross-browser compatibility: Includes specifically tuned, ready-to-use configuration files for Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Brave.
Multi-OS deployment scripts: Provides easy-to-use installation scripts and detailed manual guides for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Telemetry blocking: Completely severs background data reporting and analytics connections to the respective browser developers.
AI feature stripping: Forcibly removes integrated AI tools, shopping assistants, and sidebars that clutter the modern browsing UI.

useCases.title: Edge debloating
useCases.description: Removes the Copilot integration, shopping features, and sponsored new tab content from Microsoft Edge on Windows machines.

useCases.title: Privacy hardening
useCases.description: Applies strict enterprise policies to Firefox to ensure absolutely zero telemetry data is transmitted back to Mozilla servers.

useCases.title: Corporate workstation setup
useCases.description: Provides system administrators with a baseline configuration to deploy distraction-free, secure browsers across company devices.

useCases.title: Minimalist browsing restoration
useCases.description: Allows users to restore a fast, classic browsing experience without the distraction of modern sidebar widgets and integrations.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Privacy advocates, system administrators, and minimalists who require a clean browsing experience and possess administrative access to apply system-wide policies.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Follow the OS-specific install scripts provided in the repository's documentation.
